mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 10-year average compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0% (measured over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points over one month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) relative to their 3-month moving averages indicates broad-based consumer demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline relative to their 3-month moving averages (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During early-cycle expansion (indicated by INDPRO growth above 1.5% year-over-year), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days as industrial momentum supports corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods classified as early-cycle expansion (INDPRO growth > 1.5% YoY) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent inflation above 3.5% year-over-year (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Strong nonfarm payrolls growth (PAYEMS) consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive (over a 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (indicated by GDPC1 growth above 2.0% year-over-year), the S&P 500 tends to produce negative returns over the next 60 trading days as economic peaks trigger Fed tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% YoY) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP growth (GDPC1) signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline (over a 3-year rolling window).
